set.body:
VERIFIED: no citations anywhere in user-facing documentation. No Kriegeskorte, no Diedrichsen, no Walther, no DOI, no 'et al' across README.md and both vignettes.

The specific cost, and it is the cheapest high-value fix identified in this entire review:

  'geometry' is used from README.md:4 onward and is NEVER connected to anything the reader
  already knows. It is the condition x condition SECOND-MOMENT MATRIX G. That object has two
  well-established names in this literature - 'representational geometry' (Kriegeskorte) and
  'the second-moment matrix G' (Diedrichsen, PCM) - and the package uses a TRUNCATED FORM OF
  THE STANDARD TERM without ever linking it.

  Likewise 'RSA' is used at introduction.Rmd:150 with the acronym never expanded, and
  'representational similarity' is never spelled out in full anywhere in the corpus.

So the package's central object already has a name its audience knows, and the docs use 80
percent of that name while withholding the connection. A reader who has read Kriegeskorte or
used PCM has every prerequisite for this package and is given no signal that they do.

ONE SENTENCE FIXES THE LARGEST SINGLE PIECE OF THIS, something like: 'geometry here is the
condition-by-condition second-moment matrix G of the representational geometry literature;
the RDM is a fixed linear transform of it.' The second clause matters as much as the first,
because introduction.Rmd:131 already states that squared distances are a fixed linear
transform of geometry, and a reader who knows the RDM/G relationship would recognise the
whole framework from that one sentence.

WHY THIS RANKS HIGH DESPITE BEING TRIVIAL TO FIX. Every other accessibility finding in this
workstream costs real work - a generator, a restructured vignette, a pkgdown reference,
retitled sections. This one costs a sentence and it converts the package's central noun from
'unfamiliar invented term' to 'the thing you already use, computed a better way'. It is the
highest ratio of adoption gained to effort spent that has come out of this review.

RELATED, same class, from the reviewer's inventory: three different names are used for one
never-defined concept - 'evidence pairing' (README.md:12), 'evidence form'
(evidence-pairing.Rmd:2), 'evidence operator' (DESCRIPTION:9). None of the three is defined
anywhere, and one of them is the vignette's own filename. Pick one and define it once.

NOT PROPOSING a literature review or a related-work section. A handful of anchor citations at
the points where the package's objects coincide with named objects in the field. The absence
of citations is not a scholarly failing here; it is a NAVIGATIONAL one.
set.title: Zero literature anchors in 1263 lines: 'geometry' is never connected to the second-moment matrix G
